preamble: Pharyngealization of the uvular ejective: in Nuu-chah-nulth (Nootka), Proto-Southern-Wakashan *qʼ and *qʼʷ merged into the pharyngeal /ʕ/, while plain *χ became /ħ/ (Jacobsen 1969). Ditidaht shares the change except after consonants, where qʼ survives; Makah keeps qʼ. Phonetically the Nuu-chah-nulth reflex is a pharyngealized glottal or epiglottal stop, so the glottal closure of the ejective is retained while the uvular closure retracts to the pharynx.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Southern Wakashan to Nuu-chah-nulth and Ditidaht

examples.note: Northern Wakashan cognates (Heiltsuk, Kwakʼwala) have qʼʷ.
Makah form as in Davidson (2002: 76), ex. (127), which pairs it with Nuu-chah-nulth ʔ̴uy̓i.
Synchronic hardening of plain /q/ after a consonant (Werle 2010, ex. 56), which is why Ditidaht shows qʼ rather than ʕ in this position.
